solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This person occupying the old-fashioned province as an Arab

indicators.note: one piece occupying another sits inside it, so ME goes into the other letters

parts.note: YE is the archaic form of the
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
the setter calling himself this person gives ME

explanation.surface: Someone describes living in a quaint old province as an Arab.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is commonly called the Province in Britain; YE is the mock-antique spelling of 'the', as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Yemen, on the Arabian peninsula, is an Arab by nationality.

clue.text: Support reduced when Right gets in with children going under

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece going under another follows it
Right gets in means its letter is placed inside the word for reduced

parts.note: a price that is reduced has been cut

explanation.surface: Welfare support is cut when a right-wing government takes over, with children suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right gets in' reads like politics, but it only inserts a letter; in a down entry 'going under' means the last piece follows below.
explanation.definitionFit: A crutch is a prop that gives physical support to someone who is lame.

clue.text: Novelist making rotten bachelor reform — about time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the time letter
to reform is to reshape, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novelist turns a rotten bachelor into a reformed man, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rake reformed, but 'reform' is the anagram signal and 'about' wraps the shuffled letters round the time abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Jane Eyre was one of the three Brontë sisters, all novelists.

clue.text: Cut off — one thus gets behind schedule

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means thus, in this way
something behind schedule is late

explanation.surface: Someone running behind schedule finds himself cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cut off from others is to be separated, set apart alone.

clue.text: This officer in short could appear to be politically correct

definitions.text: This officer in short could appear to be politically correct

parts.words: This officer in short could appear to be politically correct
parts.note: the abbreviation for this police rank is the same two letters, P and C, used for politically correct

explanation.surface: A policeman's short title makes him seem politically correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Both phrases shorten to PC, so the officer's abbreviated title looks like the label for politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest rank in a British police force, abbreviated PC, is a uniformed officer.

clue.text: Very good sailor? Not if he's doing this!

definitions.text: Very good sailor? Not if he's doing this!

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword slang for very good
a rating is an ordinary sailor in the navy

explanation.surface: A sailor caught doing this could hardly be called very good.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a sailor engaged in robbery at sea is no very good sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbing ships at sea is what a buccaneer does, hardly the act of a virtuous seaman.

clue.text: Secret man, I care to be devious

indicators.note: devious means winding and indirect, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A secretive man admits he likes to be devious.
explanation.definitionFit: Proceedings held behind closed doors, in private chambers, are secret from the public.

clue.text: Examines notices either side of bridge

indicators.note: the notices word sits on either side of the bridge word, enclosing it

parts.note: to notice something is to see it
an arch is the span of a bridge

explanation.surface: An inspector examines notices posted at each end of a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notices' looks like a noun for posted signs; it is the verb, split in two to sit at each end of the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To search something is to examine it thoroughly, looking for what is hidden.

clue.text: China perhaps and gold that is linked to part of Scripture

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Gold from China is linked to a passage of the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China perhaps' defines by example: China is one country of the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The East, home of China, Japan and their neighbours, is traditionally called this.

clue.text: Bird nesting in window ledge

indicators.note: something nesting in these words is tucked inside them, spanning the two

explanation.surface: A bird has made its nest on a window ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: This nocturnal hooting raptor is a bird of prey.

clue.text: Nibbled, we hear, and said to be sort of cross

indicators.note: we hear marks a word chosen for its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a bird that nibbled has pecked
oral means spoken, said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone nibbled at food and, by all accounts, became rather cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' gives the sound of PECKED, spelt PECT. A pectoral cross is the one a bishop wears on the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's chest-worn crucifix is called by this adjective, meaning of the breast.

clue.text: At home, then not at home to some extent

parts.note: someone in is at home
someone away is not at home

explanation.surface: Someone is home, then not home, so only partly there.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means partly, in a certain sense or degree.

clue.text: Sort of good time that rooftop prisoners have in the dark?

definitions.text: Sort of good time that rooftop prisoners have in the dark?

parts.words: Sort of good time that rooftop prisoners have in the dark?
parts.note: read literally, people trapped on the roof spend their dark hours up among the slates; idiomatically, a riotous evening out

explanation.surface: Prisoners stuck on a rooftop at night are having a strange kind of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a wild evening of revelry, like cats roaming roofs at night.

clue.text: Tribe of Israel to wander about

definitions.meaning: one of the twelve tribes, descended from a son of Jacob
a verb meaning to roam aimlessly

explanation.definitionFit: One of Jacob's sons founded a tribe of that name, and the verb means roam idly.

clue.text: An Italian poet's movement not showing any sign of hurry

definitions.text: movement not showing any sign of hurry

parts.note: Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An Italian poet walks along without any sign of being in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical movement marked at a moderate walking pace is unhurried.

clue.text: Winding up Miss Heather

parts.note: to miss something is to need or want it
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: Someone is teasing a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Heather' looks like a woman's title and name; it splits into the verb miss and the plant heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Winding someone up is British slang for teasing or provoking them.

clue.text: Showing sagacity, like archbishop briefly coming to cathedral

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: a name given briefly is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Desmond Tutu was Archbishop of Cape Town
Ely is an English cathedral city

explanation.surface: A clever archbishop pays a quick visit to a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims TUTU to TUT. Ely, in Cambridgeshire, is a cathedral city often met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting shrewdly and cleverly is acting with sagacity.

clue.text: Man's man?

definitions.meaning: the capital of the Isle of Man, that island's chief town

explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man's capital town shares its name with a common masculine first name.

clue.text: Floral arrangement that is left up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A flower arrangement that is left up on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IE + L backwards in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck is a floral arrangement.

clue.text: Criminal — for instance, gangster, bad at the outset

parts.note: ill means bad, and at the outset places it first
EG, exempli gratia, means for instance
Al Capone is the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A gangster, for instance, is a criminal who was bad from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order runs instance, gangster, bad, but 'at the outset' asks for the bad word first; Al Capone is the stock crossword gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Something criminal is against the law, unlawful.

clue.text: Italian debt is so bad — so will Eurozone suffer this?

indicators.note: bad signals the letters are in a bad, disordered state and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Italy's debt is so bad that the whole Eurozone may suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettling a system, making it unstable, is what bad debt threatens the currency bloc with.

clue.text: Military entertainment that gets under the skin

definitions.meaning: a display of marching and music by troops, as at Edinburgh
ink pricked into the skin as a design

explanation.definitionFit: Both a forces pageant and a skin design inked with needles share this name.

clue.text: Having to confess in front of gathering

parts.note: to own up is to confess

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone has to confess in front of a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning something means possessing it, having it as yours.

clue.text: Fate of idiot with hope half gone

parts.note: a clot is British slang for an idiot

indicators.note: with half gone only the first two of the four letters stay

explanation.surface: An idiot's fate is to have half his hope gone.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the three Fates of Greek myth, the one who spins the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology she is one of the three Fates, the spinner of life's thread.

clue.text: No longer performing on stage? That's tough

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
acting is performing in a play

explanation.surface: A retired actor finds life tough.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding, tough task is one that asks a great deal.

clue.text: It's no good harbouring a worry constantly

indicators.note: harbouring means holding inside, so the letters go round the article

explanation.surface: It does no good to keep fretting over a worry.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag is to pester or fret at someone continually.

clue.text: Ornament showing mammal rolling over captured by worker

indicators.note: a piece captured by another is held inside it

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker

indicators.note: rolling over turns the mammal word backwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer, a mammal

explanation.surface: A worker displays an ornament showing a mammal rolling over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling over' reverses the deer, giving KLE, and 'captured by' places that inside the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain or band worn round the ankle is a piece of ornament.

clue.text: Complete description of shapes lacking any angularity?

definitions.text: description of shapes lacking any angularity?
definitions.meaning: shapes without corners are wholly curved, every one circular

explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated word means versatile and complete; split, it says every shape is circular.
